title: Everyday verbs 2
about: Verbs for changes: when English uses go, turn, become, fall or grow instead of get (go bald, turn red, become extinct, fall ill, grow older), and common get mistakes to avoid, such as get friends instead of make friends.

items.pattern: go mad · go mad with worry / boredom · (BrE, informal) go mad = get very angry
items.meaning: become mentally ill; in everyday speech, become extremely bored, worried or angry
items.example: Our neighbour's dog barks all night. I'm going to **go mad**.
more: Dad will **go mad** when he sees the scratch on his car.
After a month of rain, we were all **going mad** indoors.
items.watchOut: «Збожеволіти» — go mad. Became mad звучить неприродно, а get mad у розмові (особливо американській) зазвичай означає «розсердитися». Британці й про сильний гнів кажуть go mad: Mum went mad — мама страшенно розлютилася.

items.pattern: go bald · be going bald · go bald early
items.meaning: lose the hair on your head
items.example: My brother started **going bald** at twenty-five, so now he shaves his head.
more: All the men in my family **go bald** early.
He's worried about **going bald** before his wedding.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай кажуть go bald, а не get bald чи become bald. Вимова: bald /bɔːld/, як ball, а не /bæld/.

items.pattern: go grey · turn grey · be going grey
items.meaning: start to have grey hair
items.example: My mum **went grey** in her forties but never dyed her hair.
more: Our old dog has **gone grey** around the nose.
Stop worrying so much, or you'll **go grey**!
items.watchOut: «Посивіти» — go grey або turn grey; became grey звучить книжно. Британське написання — grey, американське — gray.

items.pattern: go blind (in one eye) · become blind (formal)
items.meaning: lose the ability to see
items.example: Our old cat **went blind**, but she still finds her way round the flat.
more: Never look straight at the sun, or you could **go blind**.
Uncle Petro **went blind in one eye** after a fireworks accident.
items.watchOut: «Осліпнути» — go blind, а в офіційному тексті — become blind. Get blind у цьому значенні не кажуть.

items.pattern: go deaf (in one ear) · become deaf (formal)
items.meaning: lose the ability to hear
items.example: My uncle worked in a noisy factory for years and slowly **went deaf**.
more: Turn that music down or you'll **go deaf**!
Grandad pretends he's **gone deaf** whenever we ask him to help with the washing-up.
items.watchOut: Вимова: deaf /def/, як left, а не /diːf/. «Оглухнути» — go deaf (офіційно become deaf). Про поступову зміну в розмові буває he's getting a bit deaf, але про те, що вже сталося, кажуть went deaf.

items.pattern: go (bright) red · sb's face goes red · also turn red
items.meaning: suddenly become red in the face because you are embarrassed, angry or hot
items.example: When the waiter sang 'Happy Birthday', my sister **went bright red**.
more: He **goes red** every time someone mentions his ex-girlfriend.
Dad's face **went red** with anger when he saw the parking ticket.
items.watchOut: «Почервоніти» — go red або turn red; became red звучить штучно. Почервоніти від сорому — ще й blush.

items.pattern: the sky / room / screen goes dark · it's getting dark (in the evening)
items.meaning: suddenly become dark
items.example: In the middle of the film, the cinema screen **went dark** and the sound stopped.
more: At the end of the play the stage **went dark** and everyone started clapping.
When the sun disappeared behind the clouds, the lake **went dark** and cold.
items.watchOut: Про вечір, коли темніє поступово, зазвичай кажуть it's getting dark. Go dark — про раптову зміну: the room went dark, the screen went dark.

items.pattern: sth goes yellow / brown (with age / in the sun) · also turn yellow / brown
items.meaning: slowly change colour because of age, sun or air
items.example: The old letters in Grandma's drawer have **gone yellow** at the edges.
more: Bananas **go brown** quickly in the fridge.
The white curtains **went yellow** in the sun, so I bought new ones.
items.watchOut: Повільна зміна кольору від часу, сонця чи повітря — go yellow / brown (або turn yellow / brown). Became yellow кажуть рідко.

items.pattern: sth turns gold / pink / orange (the sky, the sea, leaves, fields)
items.meaning: become a golden colour, like the sky at sunset or leaves in autumn
items.example: In October the birch trees in the park **turn gold**.
more: We sat on the beach and watched the sea **turn gold**, then pink.
After a summer at the seaside, my daughter's hair had **turned gold**.
items.watchOut: Зміну кольору в природі описують через turn (у британській розмовній ще go): the leaves turned gold. Got gold так не кажуть.

items.pattern: sth turns red (fruit, leaves, traffic lights) · also go red
items.meaning: become red, especially as part of a natural change such as fruit ripening
items.uk: почервоніти, стати червоним (про плоди, листя, світлофор)
items.example: Leave the green peppers on the windowsill and they'll **turn red** in a few days.
more: My nose **turns red** as soon as it gets cold.
By the end of the summer the rowan berries had **turned red**.
items.watchOut: Про стиглі плоди, листя чи світлофор — turn red, а в британській розмовній часто go red: the lights went red.

items.pattern: sb's hair turns white · sb's face turns / goes white (with shock or fear)
items.meaning: become white; a face turns white with shock or fear, hair turns white with age
items.example: When she saw the size of the bill, her face **turned white**.
more: My grandad's hair **turned white** when he was only fifty.
The sea **turned white** with foam as the wind picked up.
items.watchOut: «Зблід» — his face turned white / went white або went pale. Про волосся: з сивиною — grey, зовсім біле — white.

items.pattern: become / get pregnant (with twins / with your first child)
items.meaning: start to carry a baby inside your body
items.example: My cousin **became pregnant** with twins, and the whole family was thrilled.
more: She **became pregnant** a month before her wedding.
They'd been trying for years before she finally **got pregnant**.
items.watchOut: У розмові найчастіше get pregnant, в офіційних текстах — become pregnant, у британській розмовній трапляється fall pregnant. Усі три правильні.

items.pattern: become / get involved in sth / with sb
items.meaning: start to take part in an activity, group or organisation
items.example: After she retired, my aunt **became involved in** a local animal shelter.
more: Parents are welcome to **get involved in** the school's summer fair.
My brother **became involved with** a theatre group at university.
items.watchOut: «Долучитися до чогось» — become / get involved IN sth, а не involved to. Get involved — розмовно, become involved — офіційніше.

items.pattern: become / get angry (with sb / about sth) · become / get upset (about sth)
items.meaning: start to feel angry, or unhappy and worried
items.example: The passengers **became angry** when the train was delayed for the third time.
more: My little sister **gets upset** if you don't let her win.
The shop assistant stayed calm even when the customer **became angry**.
items.watchOut: Сердитися на когось — angry WITH sb (американці частіше кажуть at), але не angry on sb. Засмутитися через щось — upset ABOUT sth. У розмові частіше get angry / get upset.

items.pattern: become / get excited (about sth)
items.meaning: start to feel very happy and enthusiastic about something good
items.example: The kids **became excited** as soon as they saw the snow.
more: Don't **get too excited**. We haven't won anything yet.
My grandparents **became very excited** when we told them about the baby.
items.watchOut: Excited — радісне хвилювання, передчуття. Якщо хвилюєшся перед іспитом (тривожишся) — nervous або worried, а не excited. І не плутай: I'm excited — я в захваті; it's exciting — це захопливо.

items.pattern: become / get bored (with sth) · become / grow impatient (with sb)
items.meaning: start to feel bored, or start to lose your patience
items.example: After an hour in the queue, people started to **become impatient**.
more: Kids **get bored** quickly on long car journeys.
Dad soon **became impatient** with the slow service and asked for the bill.
items.watchOut: «Мені нудно» — I'm bored, а не I'm boring (boring — нудний, такий, що наганяє нудьгу). Impatient WITH sb, bored WITH sth.

items.pattern: become / get depressed (about sth)
items.meaning: start to feel very unhappy, often for a long time
items.example: During the long, grey winter, my flatmate **became quite depressed**.
more: Don't **get depressed** about one bad mark. You'll do better next time.
Many older people **become depressed** when they live alone and rarely go out.
items.watchOut: «Впасти в депресію» — не fell depressed. Кажуть become depressed (розм. get depressed) або fall into depression.

items.pattern: become / get / turn violent
items.meaning: start to behave in a way that hurts people or damages things
items.example: The man **became violent** when the bar staff refused to serve him, so they called the police.
more: The argument in the street **turned violent**, so we crossed to the other side.
Teachers are trained to stay calm if a pupil **becomes violent**.
items.watchOut: Violent — про фізичну агресію: б'ються, ламають речі. Aggressive ширше: може бути й про грубі слова чи манеру. Протест, що «переріс у сутички», — turned violent.

items.pattern: become extinct · also go extinct, die out
items.meaning: stop existing because the last animals or plants of that kind have died
items.example: Without the national park, these wild cats might **become extinct**.
more: The dodo **became extinct** in the 17th century.
Some old apple varieties have almost **become extinct**.
items.watchOut: «Вимерти» — become extinct або die out; get extinct — помилка. Американці й журналісти часто кажуть go extinct. Наголос на другому складі: ex-TINCT.

items.pattern: become popular / unpopular (with sb)
items.meaning: start to be liked (or disliked) by a lot of people
items.example: Cycling to work has **become popular** in our town since they built new bike lanes.
more: The new head teacher quickly **became popular with** the parents.
The mayor **became unpopular** after he closed the local swimming pool.
items.watchOut: У розмові можна сказати get popular, але в листі чи есе краще become popular. Популярний серед когось — popular WITH sb (або among sb).

items.pattern: become homeless · be made / left homeless (by a flood, a fire)
items.meaning: lose the place where you live and have nowhere to live
items.uk: залишитися без даху над головою, стати безхатьком
items.example: When the factory closed, my uncle lost his flat and nearly **became homeless**.
more: Dozens of families **were left homeless** after the river flooded.
A friend let him sleep on her sofa so he wouldn't **become homeless**.
items.watchOut: «Залишилися без житла» — became homeless або were left / made homeless; не stayed homeless і не got homeless.

items.pattern: become famous (for sth / as sth)
items.meaning: start to be known by a lot of people
items.example: The small fishing village **became famous** when a film was shot there.
more: She **became famous as** a TV cook in the nineties.
The beach **became famous for** its pink sand after it appeared in a travel magazine.
items.watchOut: У розмові кажуть і get famous, але в есе й листах — become famous. Прославитися чимось — become famous FOR sth, як хтось — AS sb.

items.pattern: fall ill · fall sick · also get ill, be taken ill
items.meaning: become ill, often suddenly
items.example: Half the class **fell ill** with flu the week before the school trip.
more: Our cat **fell ill** after eating a lily from the garden.
Dad **fell ill** on the first day of our holiday and spent it in bed.
items.watchOut: Fall ill звучить трохи офіційніше; у розмові частіше get ill або be ill. Went ill так не кажуть. І не плутай з feel ill — почуватися погано.

items.pattern: fall silent · also go quiet / go silent
items.meaning: suddenly stop talking or making a noise
items.example: The whole restaurant **fell silent** when a waiter dropped a tray of glasses.
more: When I asked who had eaten the last piece of cake, the kids **fell silent**.
The birds **fell silent** just before the storm.
items.watchOut: «Замовкнути» — fall silent або go quiet. Became silent теж можна, але звучить книжно.

items.pattern: grow older · grow old (together) · (informal) get older
items.meaning: become older as time passes
items.example: My parents want to **grow old** in the village where they met.
more: Our dog has **grown old** and doesn't want long walks any more.
Strangely, I like spicy food more now that I've **grown older**.
items.watchOut: «З віком» — as you grow older (розм. get older). Turn — про конкретний вік: she turned forty — їй виповнилося сорок.

items.pattern: grow + comparative: grow louder / colder / stronger / darker
items.meaning: gradually become louder (or colder, stronger…)
items.example: The music from next door **grew louder** as the party went on.
more: The smell of smoke **grew stronger** as we walked towards the village.
The evenings **grow colder** in October, so we light the fire.
items.watchOut: Grow + вищий ступінь (louder, colder, stronger) — поступова зміна, звучить трохи книжно. У розмові частіше get louder / get colder.

items.pattern: make (new) friends · make friends with sb
items.meaning: start new friendships
items.example: On my language course I **made new friends** from five different countries.
more: She's very shy and finds it hard to **make friends**.
We **made friends with** a lovely couple on holiday in Greece.
items.watchOut: «Завести друзів» — make friends, не get friends. Find friends теж трапляється, але звичайне сполучення — make friends. «Подружитися з кимось» — make friends WITH sb.

items.pattern: have / suffer a (mild / serious) heart attack
items.meaning: have a sudden, serious problem with your heart
items.uk: у когось стався інфаркт; перенести інфаркт
items.example: Our neighbour **had a heart attack** while he was clearing snow from his drive.
more: Doctors say he **suffered a mild heart attack** and will be fine.
My grandfather **had a heart attack** at sixty and changed his diet completely.
items.watchOut: Не got a heart attack. Кажуть had a heart attack, у новинах і в лікарів — suffered a heart attack. Так само про інсульт: he had a stroke — у нього стався інсульт.

items.pattern: have a child / children (of your own)
items.meaning: become a parent; have sons or daughters
items.example: My grandparents **had five children**, so family dinners are always noisy.
more: She'd love to **have a child of her own** one day.
Do you think you'll ever **have children**?
items.watchOut: Не get a child / get children. «Скільки у вас дітей?» — How many children do you have?

items.pattern: go crazy (with boredom / worry) · the crowd went crazy
items.meaning: lose control of your mind; informally, become very excited, bored or angry
items.example: When the band came on stage, the crowd **went crazy**.
more: If I have to stay in this hotel room one more day, I'll **go crazy**.
My little brother **goes crazy** for anything with chocolate in it.
items.watchOut: Не I'm getting crazy. «Я божеволію» — I'm going crazy. Get crazy буває хіба в значенні «відірватися, розійтися» (Let's get crazy tonight!) або про ситуацію (things got crazy).

items.pattern: have a baby (girl / boy) · be having a baby
items.meaning: give birth to a baby; be expecting one
items.uk: народити дитину; чекати дитину (be having a baby)
items.example: My best friend **had a baby girl** last Tuesday.
more: She **had her baby** at home, with a midwife.
My parents **had a baby** when I was ten, so I've got a much younger brother.
items.watchOut: Не got a baby. «Народила» — had a baby або gave birth to a baby. Born — тільки was born: The baby was born at night.

warmup.uk: Він мало не збожеволів від хвилювання, коли донька не повернулася вчасно додому.
warmup.q: He nearly ___ mad with worry when his daughter didn't come home on time.
warmup.explain: Збожеволіти — go mad (від хвилювання — go mad with worry). Get mad у розмові означає «розсердитися», а turn mad так не кажуть.

warmup.q: Without the operation he could ___ blind.
warmup.explain: Осліпнути — go blind (офіційно become blind). Get blind і turn blind так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Коли він утратив роботу, то впав у депресію.
warmup.q: After he lost his job, he ___ depressed.
warmup.explain: Впасти в депресію — не fell depressed. Кажуть became depressed (розм. got depressed) або fell into depression.

warmup.uk: Цей вид риби вимер, бо річку забруднили.
warmup.q: This kind of fish ___ extinct because the river was polluted.
warmup.explain: Вимерти — become extinct (також go extinct) або die out. Got extinct і died extinct — помилки.

warmup.uk: Після пожежі в будинку десять сімей залишилися без житла.
warmup.q: Ten families ___ homeless after the fire in their block of flats.
warmup.explain: Залишитися без житла — become homeless або be left homeless. Got homeless і fell homeless — помилки.

warmup.uk: У новому місті вона швидко завела нових друзів.
warmup.q: She quickly ___ new friends in her new town.
warmup.explain: Завести друзів — make friends. Get friends — типова помилка.

warmup.uk: Торік у мого дядька стався інфаркт.
warmup.q: My uncle ___ a heart attack last year.
warmup.explain: Інфаркт «стається» — have a heart attack (офіційно suffer a heart attack). Не got і не caught.

warmup.q: When did you ___ your first baby?
warmup.explain: Народити — have a baby або give birth to a baby. Born — тільки was born: I was born in 1990. Get a baby — помилка (так кажуть хіба про усиновлення).

A.q: After a bad ear infection, the little girl ___ deaf in one ear.
A.explain: Про те, що вже сталося, кажуть went deaf (офіційно became deaf). Got deaf і turned deaf так не кажуть.

A.q: Dad says his hair went ___ because of us kids.
A.explain: Про волосся — go grey (посивіти) або turn grey.

A.q: Mum says Dad was already ___ bald when they met.
A.explain: Лисіти — go bald: he was going bald. Turn і fall із bald не вживають.

B.q: The apples on our tree are starting to turn ___, so we'll pick them soon.
B.explain: Стиглі яблука червоніють — turn red (або go red).

B.q: Her hair turned ___ very early, so people often think she's older than she is.
B.explain: Зовсім біле волосся — white, із сивиною — grey. Обидва кольори видають вік.

B.q: Look! The clouds have ___ gold and pink.
B.explain: Колір змінюється — turn gold (у британській розмовній ще go gold). Get gold так не кажуть.

C.q: Some languages ___ extinct when their last speakers die.
C.explain: Вимерти — become extinct (а також go extinct або die out). Get extinct — помилка.

C.q: Lots of students become involved ___ volunteering during the summer.
C.explain: Долучитися до чогось — become involved IN sth, не to.

C.q: Our local football team ___ famous when they beat the national champions.
C.explain: Прославитися — become famous (розм. get famous). Made famous потребує додатка: the win made them famous.

D.q: Everyone in the waiting room ___ silent when the doctor came out with the results.
D.explain: Замовкнути — fall silent (або go quiet). Make і have тут не підходять.

D.q: Our teacher ___ ill, so a supply teacher took our class for two weeks.
D.explain: Захворіти — fall ill (або get ill). Went ill і turned ill так не кажуть.

D.q: As the children grew ___, they needed bigger bedrooms.

E.q: Our kids ___ new friends at the campsite on the very first day.
They've been married for ten years and they'd like to ___ a child soon.
E.explain: Мати дитину, народити — have a child. Get a child — помилка.

E.q: After three hours in a traffic jam with two small children, I was ___ crazy.
E.explain: Божеволіти — go crazy: I was going crazy. Getting crazy і becoming crazy носії так не кажуть.

example.title: Back to the village
example.uk:
Минулого жовтня я їздив до бабусі й дідуся в село. Дерева на пагорбах позолотіли, а старі фотографії на стінах пожовкли.

Дідусь зовсім облисів і почав трохи глухнути, тож за вечерею ми всі кричали. Бабуся розповіла, що моя двоюрідна сестра щойно народила дитину, а сільський хор прославився після одного телешоу.

Потім у всьому будинку раптом потемніло: зникло світло. На мить усі замовкли, а тоді дідусь почав розповідати страшні історії. Мій молодший брат густо почервонів, коли ми знайшли його під столом: історії його налякали.

Що старшими стають бабуся з дідусем, то частіше я хочу їх провідувати.
example.en:
Last October I visited my grandparents in their village. The trees on the hills had [[turned gold|b1]], and the old photos on their walls had [[gone yellow|a8]].

Grandad had [[gone completely bald|a2]] and was [[going a bit deaf|a5]], so we all shouted at dinner. Grandma told me that my cousin had just [[had a baby|e5]] and that the village choir had [[become famous|c11]] after a TV show.

Then the whole house suddenly [[went dark|a7]]: a power cut. Everyone [[fell silent|d2]] for a moment, and then Grandad started telling ghost stories. My little brother [[went bright red|a6]] when we found him hiding under the table: the stories had scared him.

As my grandparents [[grow older|d3]], I want to visit them more often.
